predecessors.name: Union of Burma (Myanmar)
predecessors.text: Paletwa Township, the southern tip of Chin State on the Bangladesh frontier: 'the Arakan Army launched an offensive in Paletwa Township' on 14 November 2023 and 'Paletwa was captured in January…

ledger.x: 2024: the Arakan Army takes its first town, Paletwa, in January, two months after its offensive began: 'the Arakan Army launched an offensive in Paletwa Township' on 14 November 2023 (Myanmar civil war page) and 'Paletwa was captured in January 2024'.
2024: the Arakan front of Operation 1027 is open across Rakhine; it began on 13 November 2023 when 'the Arakan Army attacked two Border Guard Police stations in Rathedaung Township'.

2024: Mrauk-U District falls in February: Minbya on 6 February, Kyauktaw on 7 February, Mrauk-U on 10 February and Myebon about five days later (the page also says the district was fully controlled by 6 February).
2024: Thandwe Airport is captured on 23 June and Thandwe town on 17 July.

2024: Maungdaw is captured on 8 December, giving the AA the three Myanmar townships on the Bangladesh border (Maungdaw, Buthidaung, Paletwa) and 'full control over the 271-kilometer border' (Maungdaw page).
2024: Taungup falls on 13 December when the Tatmadaw's MOC-5 surrenders after 42 days of fighting.

wars.name: Arakan front of Operation 1027 (Rakhine offensive)
wars.outcome: By the end of 2024 the Arakan Army held Paletwa, Mrauk-U District, Buthidaung, Thandwe, Maungdaw and Taungup and 'most of Rakhine's territory'; Sittwe, Kyaukphyu, Ramree, Ponnagyun and Rathedaung were fought over; the Ann offensive began on 24 March 2024 and…

certainty.note: Front lines are town-based and moving; the township circles are the researcher's placement.
